title: What height does each point on the cross section show?
description: A geographical cross section with a sea level line at zero and seven marked points. Each point is read by its distance from the line, then given a plus sign above the line or a minus sign below it. The slip of reading a point below sea level as a plain number is shown with two points the same distance away on opposite sides.
teaching_notes: One idea: a height is the distance from sea level together with a sign, plus above the line and minus below it. Watch for students who read a point below sea level as a plain number without the minus sign.

video_script.why: The child reads seven heights from a cross section by finding the distance from sea level and attaching the right sign.
video_script.substitution: The book's own cross section with points A to G and its height scale in metres.
video_script.anchor: the geographical cross section of the book, with a height scale in metres and the sea level line at zero
video_script.payoff_line: A point above sea level is positive and a point below it is negative.

final_answer.spoken: eigh is plus fifteen hundred metres, B is minus five hundred, C is plus three hundred, D is minus twelve hundred, E is plus twelve hundred, F is minus two hundred and G is plus one hundred

maths_rules: sea level is the zero line, 0 m
a point above the line has a positive height; a point below the line has a negative height
distance from the line read on the scale: A 1500, B 500, C 300, D 1200, E 1200, F 200, G 100 (approximate)
above the line: A, C, E, G; below the line: B, D, F
check: D and E are both 1200 m from the line, on opposite sides, so +1200 and -1200
video_script.design: One cross section drawn from the book with the sea level line in bold at zero. Points above the line are teal, points below are amber. Distances are read first, signs come next.

<bookmark mark='slice'/>A vertical slice of land seen from the side is called a geographical cross section.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Seven points are marked on it, and the book asks for the height of each.
Which of them are higher than the sea, and which are lower?

<bookmark mark='sign'/>A place above sea level has a positive height. A place below sea level has a negative height.

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>A point above sea level is positive and a point below it is negative.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Point eigh is plus fifteen hundred metres, B is minus five hundred, and C is plus three hundred.
<bookmark mark='two'/>D is minus twelve hundred, E is plus twelve hundred, and F is minus two hundred.
<bookmark mark='three'/>G is plus one hundred metres. Each reading is approximate.
